name: RobStride 06
_comment_source: Mechanical/electrical figures from the published RobStride 06 datasheet table. Phase resistance, inductance and all thermal parameters are NOT published and are estimated by the tool - see the ASSUMED PARAMETERS section of any report.

datasheet.title: RobStride RS06 User Manual
datasheet._note: revision is the vendor's filename stamp; version/date are from the manual's own section 7 Version History. The vendor's version field is inert: the 260713 revision STILL declares v1.0 dated 2025-11-25, seven months and several real spec changes after the 251210 revision did. The sha256 is the only reliable identity - verify with 'eval_actuator.py --check-datasheets'.

gear_eff.note: back-solved from vendor Kt_out=1.09 Nm/Arms against Ke=7.6 Vrms/kRPM. Kt is quoted to 3 s.f. in the manual (1.09, not the 1.1 previously assumed), but Ke is only 2 s.f., so this stays loosely bounded

Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM.note: datasheet back-EMF, line-to-line RMS per 1000 rotor rpm

I_peak_peak_amp.note: datasheet 'max load phase current' - needs a supply that can deliver it

kt_sat_derate.note: 36 Nm actual peak vs 43.9 Nm linear extrapolation of Kt at 57 Apk; saturates harder than the RS00

tau_cont_out_spec.note: vendor 'rated load'; ambient and mounting unspecified

T_winding_max.note: 260713 revision states 145 degC (actual insulation limit 180 degC). The 251210 revision said 135 degC. This is the vendor's own design constraint, not a derived guess.

notes: Vendor rated torque of 11 N.m is quoted with no stated ambient temperature or mounting condition, so it cannot be taken as a continuous rating in an enclosed robot. This tool computes the continuous limit from the thermal model instead.
Datasheet rated-load speed is only 100 rpm at the output, far below the 480 rpm no-load figure - the rated point is a thermal limit, not a voltage limit.
Peak phase current of 57 Apk demands serious power delivery; check bus wiring and battery C-rating, not just the actuator.

Datasheet no-load speed of 480 rpm at 48 V corresponds to 4320 rotor rpm, about 97% of the line-to-line RMS the bus can supply - the RS06 runs closer to its voltage ceiling at no load than the rest of the family.
Dual 14-bit magnetic encoders, 1 Mbps CAN, FOC drive integrated. Class B insulation, -20 to 50 degC ambient, no-load current 0.98 Arms per datasheet.
Operating voltage floor is 15 V, notably lower than the 24 V of the RS00/RS01/RS02.

260713 revision adds the rated-load test setup: aluminium-alloy heat sink, 130 x 160 mm, rated load measured at 100 rpm output. The earlier 251210 revision left mounting entirely unqualified. A heat sink that size is a bench fixture, not a robot joint, so the vendor rated torque still should not be read as a continuous rating in an enclosed arm.
Vendor overload endurance (ROTATING and STALLED) is now carried as structured data in overload_curves below, where the tool cross-checks the thermal model against it.

Stall is the case to watch for holding-torque duty: the manual states single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x that when rotating, because the three phases heat unevenly with the rotor stationary. Note the stall table's rated endpoint is 8 N.m against 11 N.m rotating. The two-node thermal model assumes even heating and so reads optimistic against the stall table by construction - the report says so.
These endurance figures superseded the 251210 numbers, which differed materially (RS00 at 14 N.m: 5 s then, 3 s now). Any thermal-model fit should use the 260713 values.

overload_curves.note: 260713 manual overload endurance, rotating. Captioned 'reduced heat sink size, lower rated torque', so the heat path is worse than the 130x160 mm fixture used for the rated-torque figure.

260713 manual overload endurance, stalled. The manual states single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x that when rotating, because the three phases heat unevenly with the rotor stationary. Note the rated endpoint drops to 8 N.m against 11 N.m rotating. Use this table for holding-torque duty. The two-node model assumes even three-phase heating, so it will read optimistic here by construction.

tn_curve.note: digitised from the 260713 manual's T-N curve image (section 1.3, 48 V), read at gridline crossings; +/-1 minor division, so roughly +/-5% in torque and +/-10 rpm. Axes are labelled in this revision, unlike 251210.
